column6: lots of words for taste ... but they're limited is self-contradictory and omits salty; minor, not edited.
Garbled sentence "The honest about what the reporter experiences and feels." Changed to "The account is honest about ...".
Walden does have a chapter titled "Solitude"; verified.

Keyed false while its explanation says "This statement is actually true, not false"; Core Idea and Explainer also support disclosure and consent. Answer changed to true, misleading "False:" stem prefix removed, explanation opener changed to "This statement is true."

Keyed false while its explanation says "actually true" and the Core Idea says immersion "reduces authorial distance". Answer changed to true, "False:" stem prefix removed, explanation opener changed to "This statement is true."
Stem prefixed "True:" but keyed false (key itself is right); prefix misleads learners. Not edited.

Keyed false for "should aim for complete accuracy ... including exact dialogue"; explanation endorses approximate dialogue, in tension with standard practice that quoted words be exact and with interview-technique.md Q3. Contested, not edited.
The Armies of the Night: third-person "Mailer", October 1967 march on the Pentagon; verified.
Style only: banned word "pivotal" changed to "decisive".

Cited Maggie Nelson's The Art of Cruelty (cultural criticism) as a memoir example; changed to The Argonauts (memoir). Old Misconceptions bullets also do not follow the "- belief. (correction)" format; not edited.
Of Idleness (Essays I.8) is a real short essay on the wandering mind; verified.

Before Montaigne, rigorous writing followed formal rules overgeneralizes (Seneca's letters, Plutarch's Moralia were informal models). Explainer also says his model "has never been surpassed" (opinion). Not edited.

Keyed true that the writer "cannot alter the sequence of actual events"; explanation says "You can't rearrange events", which conflicts with the Explainer's open-then-trace-backward structure. Core Idea's "follows the actual sequence and proportions" has the same issue. Defensible if read as misrepresenting chronology, so not edited.
Named Alexis Henderson (fantasy/horror novelist) as a nature writer on grief and landscape; changed to Helen Macdonald (H is for Hawk). Old Misconceptions bullets also off-format; not edited.
Frank Sinatra Has a Cold (Talese) and Wolfe's four devices from The New Journalism introduction; verified.
